races.title: State Senate, District 43
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Brad Overcash
cands.bio: Republican attorney from Belmont, N.C. He has served in the North Carolina Senate (District 43) since January 2023. Earlier he was vice chairman of the Gaston County Republican Party, chairman of the 10th Congressional District Republican Party, treasurer of the NC Republican Party and chairman of the Gaston College Board of Trustees.
cands.gaps: We couldn't find where Brad Overcash was born or raised, or when he came to North Carolina. We found no record of the bills he sponsored, since the sponsored-legislation table on his Ballotpedia page was empty. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, guns, abortion, schools or policing, because he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in 2022, 2024 or 2026. We found no endorsements for 2024 or 2026, no controversies, and no documented foreign ties. He signed the U.S. Term Limits Pledge, but that does not match any of the platform topics.

qual.background: Attorney in private practice. qual.why: Prior legislative service (over three years in the state Senate, which writes law and the budget) combined with a law career puts him in the high range. Committee chairmanships and board seats were not counted toward the score.

cands.name: Steve Rutherford
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina Senate District 43 (Gaston County). 20-year U.S. Navy veteran, entrepreneur and documentary filmmaker. Former president of the local NAACP chapter in Charleston, SC. He has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as recommended by three online Sway voting groups: "Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress" (Vote for Peace), "Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy" (Tevin (Momala) Davis) and "Vote Against Dystopia in NC" (Kelcey).

cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace or a date for when he lived outside North Carolina during his Navy service. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws, abortion, or school vouchers and charters. His site says he helped stop a major development but does not name it, and we found no independent reporting on it. We found no official filings or actions in office, since he has not held office, and no news coverage of controversies. His site describes his education (Southern Illinois University, Dartmouth Tuck executive program, HEC Paris graduate work), but we could not verify it elsewhere.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign site calls him a son of Gaston County who graduated from South Point High School and lives in the house he grew up in, and Ballotpedia quotes him as a lifelong Gaston County resident, but no birthplace was found.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Served 20 years in the U.S. Navy, then became an entrepreneur and documentary filmmaker (the campaign site is branded Rutherford Media Group, LLC). He has held no legislative or local elected office.
qual.why: He has business-owner experience but no legislative, policy or budget career and no elected office, so he falls in the middle band. His NAACP chapter presidency is a nonprofit role and adds nothing to the score.

I will stand with local communities to protect neighborhoods, infrastructure, and quality of life, and push back against deals that put profits over people." His biography also says he was part of a grassroots coalition that stopped a major development threatening his community.
